companies.name: Google
rounds: Phone screen: 45 min, 1-2 coding questions
Onsite: 4-5 rounds — 3 coding, 1 system design (L4+), 1 behavioral
companies.notes: Expect follow-ups pushing you toward optimal complexity. Interviewers grade on problem-solving process, not just the final answer.

companies.name: Meta
rounds: Phone screen: 45 min, 2 coding questions
Onsite: 2 coding rounds (2 questions each), 1 design, 1 behavioral
companies.notes: Pace matters more than anywhere else — practice solving mediums in under 15 minutes with clean code on the first pass.

companies.name: Amazon
rounds: Online assessment: 2 coding + work simulation
Onsite loop: 4-5 rounds, every round includes Leadership Principles questions
Bar-raiser round
companies.notes: Half of every interview is behavioral — prepare 2 STAR stories per Leadership Principle and expect deep follow-up probing.

companies.name: Apple
focus_areas: Depth in your domain (teams hire directly)
rounds: Phone screen with the hiring team
Onsite: 4-6 team-specific rounds mixing coding, domain, and design
companies.notes: Interviews vary by team more than any other FAANG — research the specific team's stack and expect domain questions alongside DSA.

companies.name: Microsoft
focus_areas: Collaborative problem solving — think out loud
rounds: Phone screen: 30-45 min coding
Onsite/virtual loop: 4 rounds — coding, design, behavioral, as-appropriate round
companies.notes: Interviewers act as collaborators — engage them, take hints gracefully, and narrate your reasoning throughout.

companies.name: Netflix
focus_areas: Senior-level system design at streaming scale
rounds: Recruiter + hiring manager screens
Onsite: mixed coding/design/culture rounds, heavier on design and culture for senior roles
companies.notes: Hires almost exclusively senior engineers — expect scenario questions probing judgment, candor, and independent ownership.

companies.name: Stripe
focus_areas: Practical, real-world coding (parsing, APIs, money math)
Correctness and edge cases over algorithmic tricks
rounds: Phone screen: practical coding
Onsite: coding, integration/debugging in a real codebase, system design, hiring-manager chat
companies.notes: Famously practical: multi-part problems that grow like real requirements. Tests, edge cases, and readable code beat clever one-liners.

companies.name: Airbnb
rounds: Phone screen: 1 coding question, code must run
Onsite: 2 coding, 1 design, 2 values/experience rounds
companies.notes: Code is executed, not whiteboarded — practice writing complete, runnable programs with real test cases.

companies.name: Uber
rounds: Phone screen: 45 min coding
Onsite: 2 coding, 1 system design, 1 behavioral/hiring manager
companies.notes: Expect problems with maps, routing, and dispatch flavors — BFS on grids and heap-based scheduling come up repeatedly.

companies.name: Databricks
rounds: Phone screen: 1 hard coding question
Onsite: 2-3 coding, 1-2 systems design deep dives
companies.notes: One of the highest coding bars in the industry — drill hard-difficulty DP and heap problems under time pressure.
